title: Carry evidence envelopes across docs/evidence-only commits
body:
## Summary
Excluded from the challenge deck: re-stamping an existing envelope onto HEAD when only inert paths changed since it was built.

## Description
tools/evidence/scope.mjs (landed) now names the inert set, but every docs/evidence commit still stales all seven envelopes, because freshness is keyed on `commit`. The carry step would rewrite `commit` to HEAD and keep `builtAt`, plus a "carried from <sha>" summary suffix. The PoF product outside this repo reads `commit` as "built at", so this changes the meaning of a wire field. The critic also asked for a guard: a git-ignored input newer than the envelope (project/native/bin/*.dll, project/data/generated/city/) must block the carry.

## Flow
- decide on the PoF side whether commit may mean "valid for"
- if yes: build tools/evidence/carry.mjs with the ignored-input guard and a --fresh flag

## Expected impact
Evidence stops going stale on 60.6% of commits. Risk: PoF believes evidence ran at a commit where nothing ran.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - evidence freshness without re-running
Before: 3343 of 5520 non-merge commits since 2026-11-02 stale all envelopes
After: those commits carry (predicted)
Method: simulation - excluded before build as a cross-repo meaning change
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: carry.test.mjs over a temp git repo fixture (cases in the run deck)

title: dirtyLines() trims the first porcelain line and loses its status column
body:
## Summary
tools/lib/repo.mjs `dirtyLines` calls git() which .trim()s the whole output, so the first line " M JOURNAL.md" becomes "M JOURNAL.md".

## Description
tools/lib/repo.mjs:37 `git(...)` returns `execFileSync(...).trim()`, and dirtyLines splits that. The leading space of the first porcelain line (an unstaged modification) is lost, so a consumer that parses column 1-2 misreads it as staged. Found by the ep-a builder; tools/evidence/scope.mjs works around it. Fix: dirtyLines runs git without the trim (trimEnd only).

## Flow
- a tree with one unstaged modified file
- dirtyLines() returns ["M file"] instead of [" M file"]

## Expected impact
Porcelain consumers read the right status. Risk: a consumer that relied on the trimmed form.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality
Before: first line loses its leading space (seen in evidence/d9-seams/evidence-it10-298af5a1-dirty.log)
After: lines kept verbatim
Method: simulation - reported by a builder, not re-measured by the coordinator
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a repo.test.mjs over a temp git repo with one unstaged edit

title: Run the stricter selftest once on a GPU
body:
## Summary
tools/selftest/run.mjs now fails a windowed stage on a SCRIPT ERROR or unknown-arg warning even when its JSON says ok (dh-b), and this has not run on a GPU.

## Description
dh-b made every selftest stage go through tools/lib/dev_verdict.mjs. If today's windowed stages already print a tolerated SCRIPT ERROR, the selftest evidence kind turns red on its next run. The coordinator did not run it: the stages are windowed and need a display/GPU on a machine shared with live lanes.

## Flow
- node tools/selftest/run.mjs on a quiet machine with a display
- red: read the verdict lines, fix the script error or relax with a decision line

## Expected impact
Prevents a surprise red selftest in the next evidence run. Risk: none (read-only run).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience
Before: not run since the change
After: one green run
Method: experiment - needs a display and a quiet machine
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: run_unit --base: prove a failure pre-dates your change
body:
## Summary
The triage verdict can say UNREACHED or UNMAPPED but cannot prove a failure was already there; re-running the failing files at the merge-base would.

## Description
Runner-up of the test-suite slot B card (ts-b, landed). tools/tests/triage.mjs gives REACHED / FULL / UNMAPPED / UNREACHED from the static map. A --base mode would check out the merge-base in a temp worktree, run only the failing files there, and report "also red at base". Cost: ~40 s import per use.

## Flow
- red run -> run_unit --failed --base
- temp worktree at merge-base, run the failing files
- print "pre-existing" or "new in your change"

## Expected impact
Agents stop guessing whether a red test is theirs. Risk: temp worktree cleanup (marker-file deletion only).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one command settles "is this mine"
Before: manual checkout + rerun
After: one flag
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a test over a temp git repo where the failure exists at base vs only at HEAD
